content.title: About
content.content: Buffalo sauce is a spicy condiment made from butter, vinegar, hot sauce (usually cayenne‑based), and seasonings. It is named after Buffalo, New York, where it was first created in the 1960s as a topping for chicken wings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The original recipe was developed at the Anchor Bar in 1964.
The combination of butter and hot sauce gives a flavor that is both fiery and creamy.
Buffalo sauce is used not only on wings but also on vegetables, seafood, burgers, and even as a marinade.
There are many heat levels, from mild to extreme (the infamous "Molotov" version).
In the United States, buffalo sauce is considered a classic "game‑day" sauce, often served at football matches.

items.title: Contains capsaicin
items.content: Capsaicin in the hot sauce may boost metabolism and provide a mild analgesic effect.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Vinegar and spices contribute small amounts of B‑vitamins that support energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Butter provides vitamin E, an antioxidant that helps protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Spiciness
items.content: High capsaicin levels can irritate the stomach and esophagus in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: Butter makes the sauce calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable, especially on weight‑loss diets.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Butter may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Buffalo sauce is traditionally tossed with fried chicken wings, but it can also be added to meat marinades, burger sauces, salad dressings, or used as a dip for vegetable sticks and cheese appetizers.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the sauce in an airtight jar in the refrigerator. At 4 °C it retains flavor and quality for 2‑3 months. Before serving, let it reach room temperature so the butter does not separate.
